agent: wave 15 agent A - CValueTrigger and CIntTrigger: one field, 77 classes
question: Declare CValueTrigger and CIntTrigger and the leaves under them, so the operand at +0x40 lands on all of them with the right units; settle each leaf's size off an allocation rather than a rule; and declare CContextEffect and CTriggeredModifier.

structs.name: CValueTrigger
structs.comment:
**The base of the forty leaves whose script operand is in thousandths**, and one of the two halves of the trigger language's units question. It has no virtual table of its own - it is never instantiated - and supplies exactly one thing: slot 7, `CValueTrigger::LoadArgument` (rva 0x5D13E0), which puts `TokenToFixedPoint(text)` in `value (+0x40)`. So the number a mod writes is multiplied by 1000 with the digits after the point padded to three, and the decimal survives: `dissent = 2.5` is 2500.

**The contrast with `CIntTrigger` is the whole mod-facing point of these two declarations and a modder cannot see it from the files** - the same text `= 0.5` is half a unit under this base and zero under the other. Size 0x44: all forty leaves are allocated `push 0x44` in CTrigger::LoadKey, which is CTrigger (0x40) plus the one dword at +0x40.
structs.evidence: RTTI gives exactly 40 classes whose direct base is CValueTrigger, and `vtable.py --holding 0x9D13E0` gives exactly 40 tables holding slot 7 - the same 40 names, derived two independent ways. Size from 40 `push 0x44; call operator_new; push eax; call <ctor>` triples inside CTrigger::LoadKey (rva 0x5C8D10, 0x2296 bytes to the `ret 8` at 0x5CAFA2), each constructor identified by the vftable its body stores last. **What would show it wrong:** a 41st class deriving from it, a leaf allocated at a size other than 0x44, or any store to +0x44 by a CValueTrigger leaf's own slot 7 or Evaluate.

structs.name: CIntTrigger
structs.comment:
**The base of the thirty-seven leaves whose script operand is a plain integer**, the other half of the units question. No virtual table of its own, and it supplies slot 7, `CIntTrigger::LoadArgument` (rva 0x5D1400): `atoi(text)` into `value (+0x40)` with **no scaling at all**, or, for the two scope keywords, `arg_is_this (+0x18)` / `arg_is_from (+0x19)` and a zero value.

So an int trigger **cannot carry decimals**: `revolt_risk = 5.5` is read as 5, and `money = 0.5` under the *other* base is half a unit while the same text here would be zero. Size 0x44 for the base; 33 of the 37 leaves are allocated `push 0x44`, four have no allocation in CTrigger::LoadKey at all (their keyword falls through to a database), and `CIsCoreTrigger` - a 38th RTTI child that **overrides** slot 7 - is 0x50.
structs.evidence: RTTI gives 38 classes whose direct base is CIntTrigger; `vtable.py --holding 0x9D1400` gives 37 tables holding slot 7, and the one in the first set and not the second is CIsCoreTrigger, whose slot 7 is its own body at rva 0x5D6500 - so the two derivations agree once that override is accounted for, which is itself the reason to derive membership from the table rather than from a count. Size from 33 `push 0x44` allocations in CTrigger::LoadKey. **What would show it wrong:** another child overriding slot 7, or a leaf allocated at a size other than 0x44 while still holding 0x5D1400 at slot 7.

addresses.name: CIsCoreTrigger::LoadArgument
addresses.comment:
**Slot 7 for `is_core`, the only `CIntTrigger` child that overrides it - and the reason the keyword accepts five different kinds of argument.** 0x5D6500 to the last of four `ret 0x104` at 0x5D665C, one int3 then `CIsCoreTrigger::Evaluate` at 0x5D6660; thirteen int3 before the entry. Read end to end:

    this->is_rebels (+0x44) = 0;  this->province_id (+0x40) = 0
    if (value.type == 0x377)        this->arg_is_this (+0x18) = 1
    elif (value.type == 0x34F)      this->arg_is_from (+0x19) = 1
    elif (text == "REB")           this->is_rebels (+0x44) = 1
    elif (atoi(text) != 0)          this->province_id (+0x40) = atoi(text)
    else                            this->tag (+0x48) = CCountryDataBase::GetTag(text)

So `is_core = GER`, `is_core = this`, `is_core = from`, `is_core = REB` and `is_core = 1234` are five distinct readings of one keyword, and **nothing in the script files says so**. `REB` is the rebel pseudo-country, tested as a literal string against the constant at VA 0x15BE948 rather than resolved through the country database at all.

`this` is in ECX and the 0x104-byte `CToken` arrives by value, which is what the `ret 0x104` cleans - the same shape as the family's four shared slot-7 loaders. It was on `findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md`'s frontier as an unread slot-7 loader.
addresses.evidence: Reached from the vftable, not from a walk: `CIsCoreTrigger`'s table (VA 0x15F8160) holds this at slot 7, and `vtable.py --holding 0x9D6500` returns exactly one holder, so it is neither a fold (trap 4) nor a guessed entry (trap 2). Extent: the four `ret 0x104` all unlink the same SEH frame from `[ebp-0xC]`, and the next byte after the int3 at 0x5D665F is CIsCoreTrigger's slot 6, which the record already holds at 0x5D6660 - so the upper bound comes from the table rather than from padding. The five arms are the five exits, read in place; the tokens 0x377/0x34F are the `this`/`from` pair the record already names on CTrigger +0x18/+0x19, and atoi (0x7969F1) and CCountryDataBase::GetTag (0x118480) are both already recorded. **What would show it wrong:** a sixth exit past 0x5D665C reached by a jump from inside (trap 3) - none of the four `ret`s has a branch target beyond it - or Evaluate ignoring one of the four fields.

addresses.comment:
**The keys its switch names**, 2 of them, one case each: `potential`, `trigger`. Read from the switch by reversing/scripts/definitions.py. A loader may resolve further keys as names out of a database - CGovernment and CMinister both do - but anything that is neither is dropped in silence.

**Which block goes where**, added wave 15: neither case parses anything itself - each dispatches slot 3 (`Load`) on an embedded `CAndTrigger` and returns. `potential` (SaveToken 0x633) goes to `this + 0x48` at 0x5BAE2; `trigger` (SaveToken 0x321) goes to `this + 0x88` at 0x5BAF5. The +0x88 one is the sub-object `BuildTriggeredModifierEntry` counts for the `"%d / %d"` strip, so the figure on screen is the `trigger` block's and not the `potential` block's.
addresses.evidence: Revises the comment only - the name, signature and confidence are unchanged. The two arms read off the bytes: `cmp eax, 0x321 / je 0x5BAF5` and `cmp eax, 0x633 / je 0x5BAE2` at the head, each arm being `mov r,[ecx+N]; mov r,[r+0xC]; add ecx,N; push [ebp+8]; call r; ret 8`, with the token names from ghidra/saveTokens.json. **What would show it wrong:** the token table disagreeing about 0x321/0x633, or a third case hidden behind the fall-through to CModifier::LoadKey that also writes one of the two triggers.
addresses.revises: adds which of the two embedded CAndTriggers each key loads - the comment named both keys and said nothing about where they land, which is the half that matters now the two fields are declared

struct_fields.name: value
struct_fields.comment: **The operand, in thousandths.** Written only by slot 7 (`CValueTrigger::LoadArgument`, rva 0x5D13E0) as `TokenToFixedPoint(text)`, so `war_exhaustion = 7.5` is stored as 7500 - the same scale the savegame prints for these keys (`neutrality=88.800`, `national_unity=81.752`). A leaf's own Evaluate then either compares it straight against a thousandths field or divides it by 1000 first; findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md section 3 says which does which. **This is the opposite convention from `CIntTrigger::value` at the same offset**, and nothing in the script files distinguishes them.
struct_fields.evidence: The one writer is slot 7, already recorded `confirmed` and read end to end; 129 of the 163 triggers read `this+0x40` in their own Evaluate, which is where CTrigger's 0x40 size came from. The thousandths claim has the savegame as an independent oracle: every key a no-scaling CValueTrigger leaf reads is printed with three decimals, and every key a no-scaling CIntTrigger leaf reads is printed with none. **What would show it wrong:** a CValueTrigger leaf storing something other than the fixed-point result at +0x40, or a save writing one of those keys as a bare integer.

struct_fields.name: value
struct_fields.comment:
**The operand, as a plain integer - not thousandths.** Written only by slot 7 (`CIntTrigger::LoadArgument`, rva 0x5D1400) as `atoi(text)`, which truncates, so the decimal a mod writes is lost before anything compares it. Zeroed instead when the argument was the keyword `this` (SaveToken 0x377) or `from` (0x34F), which set `CTrigger +0x18`/`+0x19`; only 3 of the 37 leaves read those flags back, so for the other 34 `keyword = this` degenerates to `field >= 0`.

Four leaves multiply this by 1000 inside their own Evaluate because the field they compare it against is thousandths - `revolt_risk`, `pure_revolt_risk`, `nationalism`, `province_temperature` - which is the one place the script number is the natural unit and still cannot carry a fraction. **`CValueTrigger::value` is the same offset with the opposite convention.**
struct_fields.evidence: The one writer is slot 7, already recorded `confirmed` and read end to end (three `ret 0x104` exits, one function). The savegame is the independent control: `land_battles_fought=301`, `air_battles_fought=7` and `naval_battles_fought=262` are written with no decimal point and all three are read by no-scaling CIntTrigger leaves. **What would show it wrong:** a CIntTrigger leaf whose slot 7 is not 0x5D1400 and still uses +0x40 as an operand (CIsCoreTrigger is exactly that case and is declared separately), or a save writing one of these keys with decimals.

struct_fields.name: province_id
struct_fields.comment: **`is_core = <number>`: the province the condition asks about.** This is the offset `CIntTrigger` uses for its generic operand, and on this class it is not that: the class overrides slot 7 (rva 0x5D6500), which zeroes this, then writes `atoi(text)` here only when the text parses as a non-zero number. `CIsCoreTrigger::Evaluate` (0x5D6660) opens `cmp dword ptr [ecx+0x40], 0` and takes the province branch when it is set, so this field is what selects between 'is this province a core of the scope's country' and 'is the scope's province a core of the country/tag named'.
struct_fields.evidence: Read off slot 7's own body: `mov dword ptr [esi+0x40], 0` at 0x5D6525, then `call atoi(0x7969F1)` twice at 0x5D65D6/0x5D65E6 with `mov dword ptr [esi+0x40], eax` at 0x5D65EE - the first call is the test for zero and the second supplies the value. Evaluate's first instruction after the prologue reads it. **What would show it wrong:** another writer of +0x40 on this class, or Evaluate branching on it the other way round.

struct_fields.name: is_rebels
struct_fields.comment: **`is_core = REB`.** Slot 7 compares the argument text against the literal string `REB` (at VA 0x15BE948) and sets this byte instead of resolving a country tag. Zeroed by the same slot before the comparison. Three bytes of slack follow it before the tag pair at +0x48.
struct_fields.evidence: `mov byte ptr [esi+0x44], 0` at 0x5D6521 and `mov byte ptr [esi+0x44], 1` at 0x5D65BD, the latter guarded by the result of the string compare at 0x5D659F whose operand is the 'REB' literal the disassembler names. Width from the `mov byte`. **What would show it wrong:** a dword store at +0x44, or Evaluate reading +0x44 as something wider than a byte.

struct_fields.name: tag
struct_fields.comment: **`is_core = GER`: the country whose core list is tested.** The last arm of slot 7 calls `CCountryDataBase::GetTag` (rva 0x118480) and copies both halves of the result here - `mov [esi+0x48], [eax]` and `mov [esi+0x4C], [eax+4]` - which is the ordinary `CCountryTag` shape, four characters then the id. It sits at +0x48 rather than at +0x40 because this class keeps the province id and the REB flag in front of it.
struct_fields.evidence: The two stores at 0x5D6645 and 0x5D664E, from the pointer `GetTag` returns, with the lazy `CCountryDataBase` construction (`push 0x57C; operator_new; call 0x24D0`) immediately before it - the same singleton the rest of the family reads at 0x1A855A4. CCountryTag is already recorded as 0x8, char[4] then int, and 0x48 + 8 = 0x50, the allocation size. **What would show it wrong:** a third store into +0x48..+0x4F, or Evaluate comparing the characters rather than the id.

struct_fields.name: spec
struct_fields.comment: **What the script wrote on the left of `= { ... }`**, as a by-value `CEventScopeSpec` - the same 0x110-byte specification `CContextTrigger` keeps at +0x40. Built by `EventScopeSpec_Construct` (rva 0x5C1B30) from the constructor and resolved by `CEventScope::MakeScope` (rva 0x5C1C10) each time the effect runs.
struct_fields.evidence: The two `lea` of +0x20 handed to those two functions, at 0x59E288 and 0x59E2C1, and 0x20 + 0x110 = the 0x130 allocation. **What would show it wrong:** a third consumer of +0x20 that treats it as something else, or a different size for CEventScopeSpec.

struct_fields.name: name
struct_fields.comment: **The modifier's name**, the key the database looks it up by. Constructed in place - `mov [this+0x40], 0xF; mov [this+0x3C], 0; mov byte [this+0x2C], 0` is the empty short-string form (capacity 0xF at +0x14 of the string, length 0 at +0x10) - and then assigned from the constructor's second argument.
struct_fields.evidence: `lea ecx,[esi+0x2c]` followed by the capacity/length/terminator triple and `call std::string::assign (0xA160)`, at 0x5A57D-0x5A58D in LoadModifierDefinitions and again at 0x5B97E-0x5B995 in CTriggeredModifier::CTriggeredModifier, both while CStaticModifier's vftable is the one in the object. **What would show it wrong:** the triple landing at a different offset, or Hoi3CString turning out not to be 0x1C.

struct_fields.name: potential
struct_fields.comment: **The `potential = { ... }` block**, as a by-value `CAndTrigger`. `CTriggeredModifier::LoadKey` (rva 0x5BAC0) dispatches SaveToken 0x633 (`potential`) to slot 3 (`Load`) on `this + 0x48`. In HoI3 this is the gate on whether the modifier is shown or considered at all, as against `trigger`, which is whether it currently applies - but only the offset-to-keyword mapping is read off the bytes here; what the engine does with the distinction is not.
struct_fields.evidence: `mov edx,[ecx+0x48]; mov edx,[edx+0xC]; add ecx,0x48; push parse; call edx` at 0x5BAE2-0x5BAEF, under `cmp eax, 0x633`, and 0x633 is `potential` in ghidra/saveTokens.json. The sub-object itself is the CAndTrigger the constructor builds at +0x48. **What would show it wrong:** the token table being wrong about 0x633, which the pair test settles - the other arm is 0x321 `trigger` at +0x88, and the record already independently ties +0x88 to the panel's 'n / m conditions met' string.

struct_fields.name: trigger
struct_fields.comment: **The `trigger = { ... }` block**, as a by-value `CAndTrigger`. `CTriggeredModifier::LoadKey` dispatches SaveToken 0x321 (`trigger`) to slot 3 on `this + 0x88`, and this is the sub-object `BuildTriggeredModifierEntry` (rva 0x2D1130) walks through slot 11 to print `"%d / %d"` into the `modifier_strip` gui element - the only root call of trigger slot 11 in the image, once per game day per listed modifier.
struct_fields.evidence: `mov eax,[ecx+0x88]; mov eax,[eax+0xC]; add ecx,0x88; push parse; call eax` at 0x5BAF5-0x5BB08, under `cmp eax, 0x321`, and 0x321 is `trigger` in ghidra/saveTokens.json. Independently, the record already has BuildTriggeredModifierEntry taking `modifier + 0x88` by `lea` into slot 11, which is what a condition list is for. **What would show it wrong:** the two tokens being the other way round, which would also put the condition counter on `potential`.

slots_noted: CValueTrigger and CIntTrigger have no virtual table of their own (RTTI: `vftables: []` for both), so neither declaration carries a vftable_rva and neither can hold a slot record; their slot-7 bodies are already recorded under their own names, and `CTrigger`'s vftable_slots already names slot 7 `LoadArgument` for the whole family. The 76 leaf declarations introduce no function, so they need no slot records. The one new body, 0x5D6500, is slot 7 of exactly one table and is recorded under CIsCoreTrigger above.
